_about: Public-domain Henry Harbaugh (1817-1867), German Reformed pastor, Mercersburg professor and hymn writer, for the Word Hoard: The Drunkard-Maker (1849), Heaven (1853), The Heavenly Recognition (1853), The Heavenly Home (1853), Union with the Church (1856), The Life of Michael Schlatter (1857), The Fathers of the German Reformed Church, vols 1-2 (1857), The Golden Censer (1860), Poems (1860) and Treason and Law (1865), from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 56 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

harbaugh-drunkard-maker: The drunkard-maker taken from his bar to the bar of God, tried, found guilty, and condemned for murder (Office of the German Reformed Messenger, 1849)
harbaugh-heaven: Heaven; or, An earnest and scriptural inquiry into the abode of the sainted dead (Philadelphia, Lindsay and Blakiston, 1853)
harbaugh-heavenly-recognition: The heavenly recognition ; or, An earnest and scriptural discussion of the question, Will we know our friends in heaven? (Philadelphia : Lindsay and Blakiston, 1853)
harbaugh-heavenly-home: Heavenly home; or, The employments & enjoyments of the saints in heaven (Philadelphia, Lindsay, 1853)
harbaugh-union-with-church: Union with the church, the solemn duty, and the blessed privilege of all who would be saved (Philadelphia, Lindsay & Blakiston, 1856)
harbaugh-schlatter: The life of Rev. Michael Schlatter; with a full account of his travels and labors among the Germans in Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Maryland and Virginia; including his services as chaplain in the French and Indian War, and in the war of the revolution. 1716 to 1790 (Philadelphia, Lindsay and Blakiston, 1857)
harbaugh-fathers-1: The fathers of the German Reformed Church in Europe and America, vol. 1 (Lancaster : Sprenger & Westhaeffer, 1857)
harbaugh-fathers-2: The fathers of the German Reformed Church in Europe and America, vol. 2 (Lancaster : Sprenger & Westhaeffer, 1857)
harbaugh-treason-and-law: Treason and law : a discourse, delivered at Clearspring, Maryland, June 1, 1865, the day of national mourning (Philadelphia : Jas. B. Rodgers, 1865)

_excluded.harbaugh-other: Fathers of the German Reformed Church vols 3-6 (continued by D. Y. Heisler after his death); the Heidelberg Catechism edition and Sunday-school hymn books he edited
